title: Python: NB-b, a re-export hop through a differently named module file (DEC-303 (a28))
description: Filed record-only under opum-doc's ruling ODOC-640 (opum-ai/opum-doc#2065). DEC-303 (a28) item 2 (recorded in the GCLI-86 'HANDOFF 12' note): NB-b is taken as a task, run after the (a25) attribute-write rule and before step 5, so the step-5 measurement does not carry a known loss against an earlier head. Shape: from M import n where M is a module file of a DIFFERENT name than n, hop through pkg/impl.py (pkg/helper.py 'from .impl import helper' with the function behind pkg/other/helper.py). Not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Fixtures for the hop shape, red before and green after on dev, each measured by running both, with refused twins
Mutants observed red; the five-pin delta with every created or removed in-repo edge reported to opum-doc before the clear

implementationNotes: BUILT 2026-11-27 on dev 6a5ce9d7 (branch fix/GCLI-141-nb-b-reexport-hop). ROOT CAUSE: resolveImportBinding's submodule test read isModuleFileForName(binding.target, name), true for ANY target file named name.py, including the DEFINING file S3 collapsed a re-export to. isSameNameAttribute (the A4 negative guard) admitted only a SOURCE module named name.py, so `from pkg.impl import helper` (impl.py differently named, re-exporting helper from pkg/other/helper.py) was misclassified as binding the MODULE and lost resolution (nameNotBound / module-called). FIX: broaden isSameNameAttribute to admit any plain module FILE source — never a package __init__ (A4's "an __init__ is not admitted") and never a namespace directory — whose bindings resolve the name to a symbol (a def/class, directly or through a re-export); moduleBindingGate/sourceChainOutcome then follow it. This is RESOLVE-MORE, not removal-only. FIXTURES (test/python-hops.test.ts): the single differently-named hop (`from pkg.impl import helper`) and the full two-hop chain (`from pkg.helper import helper` -> pkg/impl.py -> pkg/other/helper.py) resolve to the def; refused twins (a rebound `helper = None` and a `del helper` in the middle) stay refused (rebound); a contrast preserves a true submodule import (from pkg import sub), the renamed-source hop (himpl.py) and the direct same-name A4 hop. RED-BEFORE: on dev calls.ts the 2 hop tests fail (nameNotBound) and the contrast passes; with the fix all 3 pass. MUTANTS (applied to a copy of the final src, restored after): A revert to the old source-name restriction -> the 2 hop tests red; B drop the __init__ exclusion -> A4 "a package named helper stays unresolved" red; C return true past the source-null check -> A4 "a module file that only assigns the name" and "a re-export hop through a package binds the submodule, not the function" red. Each observed subset matched its prediction. PROOF (kit /Volumes/external/archive/glyph-cli/gcli-161-proof-kit, subset155.ts sha256 90b39e0be9056b1c79649a77af527f5cb70b3fa51286db5bfe18098ddf9a0060 with +6 NB-b fixtures; dev tree origin/dev 6a5ce9d7 calls.ts 158dd883…, head tree calls.ts 807351…): RESOLVE-MORE, so compare155's removal-only subset assertion is EXPECTED to fail on created edges. Groups 1553 against floor 1553 (= 5 pins + 1394 corpus + 154 fixtures): 0 removed, 2 CREATED edges, both the intended hop `app.py:2:1->pkg/other/helper.py:helper` (single-hop and full-chain fixtures); 2 bin changes (nameNotBound -> resolvedInRepo). FIVE PINS UNMOVED (flask 1366/1366, httpx 2791/2791, jinja 2833/2833, rich 7410/7410, tqdm 981/981): 0 created and 0 removed on the pins. Controls: compare155 --control fires (2 real + 2 injected created edges, exit 0); --floor-control refuses a 1e6 floor (exit 1); compare_notes identical on all 1553 groups (and its --control fires); check-mutation blanking the created-edge assertion makes the gate wrongly PASS (exit 1->0), so the assertion is load-bearing. bun run check green (1395 tests). No DEC-182 path class; no dependency. ADJACENT, NOT BUILT (outside the `from M import n` shape): the module-attribute form `import pkg.helper; pkg.helper.helper()` still treats a from-import binding as a module in resolveModuleAttribute; it predates this change and is a separate follow-up, reported rather than widened into this task.
